No exported functions and no entry points and no initialization sequences and no access helpers appear in the fragments.

findings.text: Second generation high overlay control places its address base at bit 27 and its M selector at bit 46 and its N selector at bit 52 and its enable at bit 63. Associated masks use values 0x00003ffff8000000 and 0x000fc00000000000 and 0x00f0000000000000 and 0x8000000000000000 in base and M and N and enable order. The generic base shift yields 27 only on second generation hardware and otherwise reports an undefined revision.

One 64 bit overlay control word offers a raw view plus three identical field views for common and extended common and second generation use. Each field view reserves the low 27 bits and then provides a 19 bit writable base followed by a six bit writable M value followed by a four bit writable N value followed by seven reserved bits and a single writable enable at the top.

High overlay instance zero uses offset 0x483000 on fourth generation hardware and offset 0x1603000 on third generation hardware and zero elsewhere. High overlay instance one uses offset 0x484000 on fourth generation hardware and offset 0x1604000 on third generation hardware and zero elsewhere.

Overlay instance zero base starts at bit 26 on all listed revisions. The accelerated fourth generation variant uses a wide base mask 0x000ffffffc000000 with its M selector at bit 52 and mask 0x03f0000000000000. Both plain fourth and third generation use a narrower base mask 0x00003ffffc000000 with M at bit 46 and mask 0x000fc00000000000. Enable sits at bit 63 with mask 0x8000000000000000 on every revision. The generic base mask selects the wide value on the accelerated variant and the narrow value on plain fourth and third and zero elsewhere. The generic base shift yields 26 on plain fourth and third and negative one elsewhere.

Overlay instance zero union provides a raw 64 bit word plus five field views for common and extended common and accelerated fourth and plain fourth and third generation. Common and extended common and plain fourth and third views all reserve the low 26 bits and provide a 20 bit writable base and a six bit writable M value and a four bit N value and seven reserved bits and a single writable enable at the top. The accelerated fourth view widens the base to 26 writable bits while keeping M width and N width and uses a single undefined bit just below the top enable.

Overlay instance one repeats the same numeric scheme as instance zero. Base starts at bit 26 everywhere. The accelerated fourth generation variant uses wide base mask 0x000ffffffc000000 with M at bit 52 and mask 0x03f0000000000000. Plain fourth and third use narrow base mask 0x00003ffffc000000 with M at bit 46 and mask 0x000fc00000000000. Enable remains at bit 63 with mask 0x8000000000000000. The generic base mask picks wide on accelerated fourth and narrow on plain fourth and third and zero elsewhere. The generic base shift yields 26 on plain fourth and third and negative one elsewhere.

Overlay instance one union provides a raw 64 bit word plus five field views for common and extended common and accelerated fourth and plain fourth and third generation. Common and extended common and plain fourth and third views all reserve the low 26 bits and provide a 20 bit writable base and a six bit writable M value and a four bit N value and seven reserved bits and a single writable enable at the top. The accelerated fourth view widens the base to 26 writable bits while keeping M width and N width and uses a single undefined bit just below the top enable.

High redirect instance zero uses offset 0x483800 on fourth generation and offset 0x1603800 on third generation and zero elsewhere with a depth of 128 entries on both supported revisions and zero elsewhere. High redirect instance one uses offset 0x484800 on fourth generation and offset 0x1604800 on third generation and zero elsewhere with the same 128 entry depth on supported revisions and zero elsewhere.

Both redirect instances place their node identifier at bit zero on every revision. The accelerated fourth generation variant masks 12 bits with value 0xfff. Plain fourth and third generation mask 15 bits with value 0x7fff. Each generic node mask selects the matching per revision constant and yields zero on other hardware.

Redirect instance zero union provides a raw 64 bit word plus five field views for common and extended common and accelerated fourth and plain fourth and third generation. Common and extended common and plain fourth and third views carry a 15 bit writable node identifier in the low bits with the remaining high bits reserved. The accelerated fourth view carries a 12 bit writable node identifier in the low bits with the remaining high bits reserved.

Redirect instance one union provides a raw 64 bit word plus five field views for common and extended common and accelerated fourth and plain fourth and third generation. Common and extended common and plain fourth and third views carry a 15 bit writable node identifier in the low bits with the remaining high bits reserved. The accelerated fourth view carries a 12 bit writable node identifier in the low bits with the remaining high bits reserved.

Memory mapped register overlay control uses offset 0x480028 on fourth generation and offset 0x1600028 on both third and second generation and zero elsewhere. Base starts at bit 26 on every revision. The generic and extended base masks select wide value 0x000ffffffc000000 on the accelerated fourth variant and narrow value 0x00003ffffc000000 on plain fourth and third and second and zero elsewhere. Enable sits at bit 63 with mask 0x8000000000000000. The generic base shift yields 26 on plain fourth and third and second and negative one elsewhere.

Memory mapped register overlay union provides a raw 64 bit word plus five identical field views for common and extended common and plain fourth and third and second generation. Each view reserves the low 26 bits and provides a 20 bit writable base followed by 17 reserved bits and a single writable enable at the top.
The accelerated fourth generation GRU overlay base starts at bit 26 with a wide mask value 0x000ffffffc000000 covering 26 bits.

Real time clock uses offset 0xe0000 on fifth and fourth generation and offset 0x340000 on third and second generation and zero elsewhere. Its time field starts at bit zero with a 56 bit mask value 0x00ffffffffffffff. A separate first interrupt config uses fixed offset 0x615c0 with no revision selection.

Real time clock union provides a raw 64 bit word plus five identical field views for common and fifth and fourth and third and second generation. Each view carries a 56 bit writable clock in the low bits with eight reserved bits at the top.

Generic accessors choose values by hardware revision with explicit fallbacks. Addresses and masks fall back to zero on unsupported hardware. Base shifts for newer overlay controls fall back to negative one. One older overlay shift reports an undefined revision instead of a numeric fallback. Depths report 128 only where supported.

Base and M and enable and node identifier and clock fields are writable where shown. Low and middle and high ranges marked reserved must be treated as not usable. The N field is writable in the older second generation overlay view but appears as a plain field in newer overlay instance views. Accelerated fourth overlay views contain one undefined bit adjacent to enable. Accelerated fourth node views are narrower than other node views while accelerated fourth base views are wider than other base views.

Callers must validate generic results before use because zero address and negative one shift and undefined revision all signal unsupported hardware and must not be used as real positions. Code must not assume uniform field widths or uniform M placement because accelerated fourth hardware widens base and narrows node identifier and moves M higher than plain revisions. The single undefined bit in accelerated fourth overlay views must not be relied upon.
